subject.title: [Feature]: Memory/Context Improvements (metrics + global semantic search + conversation chaining + preload on restart)

question: Should OpenClaw treat cross-session memory, agent-facing evaluation metrics, and restart preload as separate opt-in product surfaces with explicit privacy and lifecycle contracts, rather than one umbrella implementation?
rationale: The remaining work changes what private session/workspace material is indexed and surfaced, introduces new public observability/API expectations, and may alter gateway startup behavior; source-level implementation cannot safely select those defaults.

options.title: Split into scoped decisions
options.body: Create or retain narrow tracks for session-memory policy, metrics API design, and restart preload, each with explicit acceptance and privacy boundaries.

options.title: Sponsor a unified memory program
options.body: Keep the umbrella as the implementation vehicle and assign an owner to define the combined API, privacy, and lifecycle contract before coding.

options.title: Keep all behavior opt-in
options.body: Preserve current configurable search and experimental session-memory behavior without promoting new defaults until a broader memory policy is approved.

recommendation.title: Split into scoped decisions
recommendation.body: Create or retain narrow tracks for session-memory policy, metrics API design, and restart preload, each with explicit acceptance and privacy boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work spans the memory search, usage, startup-memory, and session surfaces that must be reconciled for this decision.
